note: R2 CLAP-embedding probe. Leave-one-track-out (90 folds, group=source_id), 1800 pairs, 5 perturbation families, identical protocol to diagnose_perturbation.py (verified: this harness reproduces its published HTRS 0.849/0.829, clap_htsat 0.498/0.465, scs 0.667/0.450). L2 strength C swept per feature set and the BEST taken for each, which favours the probe (no inner CV; C is chosen on the same folds it is scored on). max_iter=5000, converged. NB max_iter=400 raised 369/540 convergence warnings on the embedding sets, but they were benign: at max_iter=5000 the C=1 numbers are unchanged (clap768_diff 0.813/0.756 either way). The probe's gain to 0.834 comes from stronger L2, not from convergence.
verdict: The strong claim ('only a decomposition can identify the edit') does NOT survive: a raw 768-d CLAP embedding difference reaches 0.834/0.776, far above any single scalar (<=0.667/0.450). The 4-dim profile still wins, by +0.026 accuracy and +0.064 macro-F1, and the margin sits in macro-F1, i.e. on the minority families where the embedding collapses. Defensible claim: 4 interpretable dimensions (20 classifier parameters) beat 768 opaque ones (3840), and those 4 are what can be attributed, ablated, re-ranked and optimised against.

readout_fidelity.note: Embeddings extracted locally under transformers 4.40; the published clap_htsat cache came from the GPU box's older build. Cosine agreement: mean |delta| 7.6e-3, max 0.103.
readout_fidelity.control: The locally recomputed cosine diagnoses at 0.496/0.471 against the published scalar's 0.498/0.465 -- the front-end version difference is irrelevant to this task.

canonical_C1.note: C=1.0, max_iter=5000, the same setting as the published diagnosis table.
